# Design System v0.2 "Highland Mist" — COP32 companion platform (unofficial)
**Status: v0.2 APPROVED visual direction (D53), Track D v2, 2026-10-03** (v0.1 was the neutral Track C proposal). Machine-readable source: `tokens.json` (generated by `build_tokens.py`; the contrast table below is the script's real output — 64 checks, 0 failures). Components: `component-inventory.md`. Review history: `redesign-directions/README.md`. Rebuild plan: `redesign-plan.md`.

## 0. Identity and honesty notes
- **v0.2 palette (D53):** misty deep teal as the single tint, lime green for the one primary action per screen, a low-sun orange accent used only decoratively, and mist/grey grouped backgrounds. The colours were **inspired by** the founder's reference image and the lime green of cic-26.com (an unverified, unofficial site). **Only colours are borrowed:** no COP32 logo, wordmark, tagline, UNFCCC mark or government mark is used (D1). A host-supplied identity, if ever granted, would replace the colour tokens only.
- **Design method:** Apple Human Interface Guidelines principles (clarity, deference, depth): large collapsing titles, grouped inset lists, translucent bars, 44px+ targets, spring feedback, true dark mode. The same structure is used on Android/web (D27); platform chrome can follow each OS.
- Every screen carries the "Independent platform — not an official COP32 product" label (IA §2.2, TRU-04).
- Basis: documentation + computed contrast. **Not** tested with real users, low-end screens or screen readers. See §10.

## 1. Principles (from D11, D16 v2, D21, D25–D27, IA second pass)
1. **Spacious and legible** — Ethiopian users report preferring spacious layouts over cluttered super-app screens; fewer items per screen, large targets.
2. **Amharic is not an afterthought** — own line-height ratio, expansion-safe labels, bundled font.
3. **Calm and trustworthy** — no ad-like banners at the top of Home, no autoplay carousels, no dark patterns (no fake urgency, no guilt copy, no pre-ticked consent; D21).
4. **Status is always visible** — source label, last-updated, offline/sync state, "TBC" as a first-class state.
5. **Never colour alone** — every status has an icon and a text label.
6. **Same structure on Android, iOS, web** (platform parity, D27); platform-native patterns only for navigation chrome.

## 2. Colour
Roles, not hues, are the API. Light and dark themes (dark uses true black with raised dark surfaces, as on iOS). A high-contrast theme is still a Should.

**Rules:** `primary` (teal) is the only tint for links, icons, selection and secondary buttons. `accent` (lime) is reserved for **one primary action per screen** and always carries `onAccent` dark ink text. Lime is never used as text on light backgrounds (it fails AA). `sunset` is decorative only (hero sun). Status colours (`info`/`success`/`warning`/`danger`) are separate from the tint. `bar`, `fill` and `separator` are translucent material values for bars, control fills and hairlines.

## 3. Typography
- **Families (v0.2):** **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** for Latin (SIL OFL; variable 200–800; designed by the Braille Institute for low-vision legibility; Latin subset ≈34 KB woff2, bundled) and **Noto Sans Ethiopic** for all Ge'ez text (bundled subset, D11). The Latin face is limited by `unicode-range`, so Ethiopic always falls through to Noto Sans Ethiopic, and `lang="am"` nodes use Noto Sans Ethiopic directly. Symbols such as ✓ → are still drawn as SVG icons only (D49). Native iOS may switch Latin text to the system font (SF Pro) after a side-by-side review; Ethiopic stays on Noto either way.
- **Weights:** 400 body, 600 row titles, 700 labels/emphasis, 800 titles. Avoid weights below 400 for Ge'ez.
- **Scale** (aligned to iOS Dynamic Type; px at 100 %; line-height ratios differ per script because Ge'ez is dense and tall):

| Style | Size | Weight | Line-height EN | Line-height AM | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| largeTitle | 34 | 800 | 1.2 | 1.4 | Screen title (collapses into the nav bar on scroll) |
| title1 | 28 | 800 | 1.2 | 1.4 | Detail-page title |
| title2 | 24 | 800 | 1.2 | 1.4 | Hero headline |
| title3 | 20 | 800 | 1.25 | 1.45 | Section header |
| headline | 17 | 600 | 1.3 | 1.6 | List-row title |
| body | 17 | 400 | 1.35 | 1.65 | Running text |
| callout | 16 | 400 | 1.35 | 1.6 | Buttons |
| subhead | 15 | 400 | 1.35 | 1.6 | Secondary lines |
| footnote | 13 | 400 | 1.35 | 1.55 | Eyebrows (uppercase, +0.04em), source labels |
| caption | 12 | 600 | 1.35 | 1.55 | Pills, tab labels (11) |

- **Tracking:** large titles −0.022em, titles −0.015em, body −0.005em; uppercase eyebrows +0.04em. Ge'ez text always 0.
- **Minimum:** body 16px; AM running text never < 14px. Honour OS text scale up to **200 %** without loss of content or function; layouts reflow, never truncate essential info (tab labels may wrap to two lines or switch to an icon-above-label stack with a 2-line cap).
- **Fallback stack:** `'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', 'Noto Sans Ethiopic', -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif` — the system fallback exists only to avoid blank text if the font fails to load; releases are blocked on font-load checks.
- **Numerals and times:** Arabic numerals by default; 24h or explicit AM/PM with `EAT` shown (Ethiopian clock counting differs — explainer to be validated); Ethiopian calendar optional (Should).
- **Language tagging:** every text node carries `lang="am"|"en"` (screen-reader voice switching).

## 4. Spacing, grid, layout
- 4-px base; scale: 0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64. Screen gutter 16; card padding 16; vertical rhythm 8/16/24.
- Content max width 720 on tablet/desktop (centered); phone is one column. Breakpoints: phone 0, tablet 600, desktop 960. Web uses top navigation at ≥ 960 and bottom tab bar below (same five destinations).
- Use **logical start/end** properties everywhere (RTL-ready for later Arabic, accessibility doc §3.2).

## 5. Shape, elevation, materials, motion
- **Radius:** 9 (icon chips, segmented control), 14 (grouped lists, cards, notices, sheets), 22 (hero, map), pill (buttons, capsules, pills).
- **Elevation:** grouped lists sit on the grey grouped background with a barely-there shadow (`e-1`); only the hero card gets a soft coloured shadow (`e-2`); sheets `e-sheet`. In dark mode, separation comes from raised surfaces, not shadow.
- **Materials:** navigation bar and tab bar are translucent (`bar` + 20px blur + 1.8 saturation) with a hairline `separator`. The nav bar is transparent at the top and turns translucent with an inline title once the large title scrolls away.
- **Motion:** 150/200/420 ms; ease `cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1)`; spring `cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1)` for press (scale .97) and the save-star pop. With reduce-motion on, all transitions and animations are removed. Nothing autoplays; the only loop is the LIVE dot pulse (also removed under reduce-motion).

## 6. Iconography
- **Lucide** (ISC licence, confirmed) outline icons as inline SVG, 24px grid, 1.75px stroke (2.15 for the selected tab), rounded joins. The prototype bundles only the 63 icons it uses (`prototype/icons.js`, ≈11 KB).
- **Icon chips:** list rows lead with a 32px rounded-square chip in a soft tone (teal, green, red, orange, blue) like iOS Settings; colour is decorative, and meaning is always carried by the text.
- **Avatars:** faceless illustrated SVG busts in token colours with varied skin tones; no photos of real or stock people.
- Icons never carry meaning alone: always a text label, except universally understood utility (search, back, alerts, profile), which still get accessible names. Mirror directional icons in RTL; do not mirror logos, media controls or clocks.

## 7. Accessibility annotations (D25–D27)
| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Target size | ≥ 48×48 dp Android, ≥ 44×44 pt iOS, ≥ 44 CSS px web (exceeds WCAG 2.2 minimum 24×24); ≥ 8 px between adjacent targets |
| Focus | Visible 3 px `focus` ring, 2 px offset, never removed; not obscured by sticky headers/tab bar (scroll-padding); logical order = visual order |
| Text scaling | Up to 200 % without clipping; fixed-height containers prohibited for text; tab bar grows; reflow at 320 CSS px (web) |
| Contrast | §2.1; re-check any new token pair with `build_tokens.py` |
| Colour | Never the only carrier of meaning; chips and banners include icon + text |
| Motion | `prefers-reduced-motion` / OS setting respected; no autoplay audio/video |
| Screen readers | Names, roles, states for every control; live-region announcements for alerts (assertive only for critical); Amharic TTS quality is uncertain → provide text and, for key content, recorded audio (Should) |
| Gestures | No path-based or multi-finger gestures required; swipe/drag always has a button alternative |
| Forms | Visible labels (not placeholders-only), inline errors with text, no time limits |
| Language | EN/AM switch in the nav bar on every screen, next to the profile button; fall back visibly ("translation pending") |
| Low data | Text-first, images ≤ 100 KB, lazy, no autoplay video; Data-saver toggle (MVP setting) |
| Privacy-by-design (D21) | No manipulative nudges; notification and location prompts are explained first and refusable; consent controls are equal-weight (Allow / Not now) |

## 8. Platform notes
Android (Material 3 navigation bar, back gesture) and iOS (tab bar, swipe-back) follow native navigation conventions with these shared tokens; implementation in whichever framework S1 selects. Tokens are exported as JSON so Android/iOS/web codebases generate platform constants from one file instead of hand-copying.

## 8a. v0.3 visual layer (D54, 2026-10-03)
Founder feedback: v0.2 read as too text-based. v0.3 keeps the tokens, palette and IA, and makes content visual:
- **Illustrated covers:** original SVG scenes, one per theme (water waves, forest, sun and solar panels, skyline, fields, terraces, rising bars, pulse line, books, shapes for youth), drawn on fixed two-colour gradients so they read in light and dark. No photos and no logos. Covers appear on session cards, visit guides, news, explainers, exhibitors, live streams and detail headers.
- **Cards and blocks first:** session cards (cover, time badge, "Open to public" badge, floating save star), image tiles with a readable dark scrim for Visit and exhibitors, news cards, people cards with large avatars, quick-action blocks (4 big icon tiles), a day picker made of date blocks, a fact-tile row on detail pages, and live cards with a large play button.
- **Shelves:** horizontal, swipeable card rows with scroll-snap on Today (Up next, Explore Addis, Featured voices) and Map (Nearby places).
- **Simple buttons:** one lime primary action per screen (48px high, pill), tinted and plain secondary buttons, and round icon buttons.
- **Interaction:** a fade-and-rise page entrance (320ms), spring press on cards and tiles (scale .97), a star "pop" when saving (saved in place, so the scroll position is kept), and a POI sheet that slides in. Everything is removed under reduce-motion.
- **Lists stay where lists are best:** Settings, glossary, library, alerts and search results keep the grouped-list style.
- At 200% text, shelves and grids become a single column and covers get fixed heights.

## 8b. Illustrated personas (D56, 2026-10-03)
Every content card carries an invented person in a themed scene (`prototype/people.js`), so the prototype reads as a real product in presentations without using photos of real or stock people.
- **Figure system:** half-body flat-vector people built from parameters: 6 skin tones; hair styles (afro, braids, bun, long, short, fade, gray, bald), head coverings (headwrap, hijab, kufi, cap); beard; glasses; shirt or jacket; a white **netela** shawl with a coloured **tibeb** border; a conference lanyard and badge; and one prop (mic, laptop, tablet, clipboard, seedling, jebena coffee pot, hard hat, camera, book, stethoscope, map, phone, plate, suitcase).
- **Cast:** 20 speakers (P01–P20, one look each, reused on their sessions, cards and avatars, so a person is recognisable across screens) and 13 roles for guides, news and live cards.
- **Rules:** every person is invented and labelled sample/fictional; the cast is diverse in gender, age and origin, with Ethiopian dress shown respectfully. No photos, no likeness of real people, no logos.
- **Photoreal option (not done):** AI-generated photoreal personas were requested. No image-generation service was available in this session (the Replicate connector failed and Figma Weave was not linked). If that is enabled later, any generated people must still be clearly marked as fictional.

## 8c. Real photos (D57, 2026-10-03)
Founder asked for real, event-like pictures instead of illustrations. Cards, features, live cards, detail headers and the Today hero now use **45 openly licensed photos** (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0) from Wikimedia Commons, found through Openverse. They show conference halls, plenaries and workshops, Addis Ababa (skyline, light rail, streets, Entoto), coffee ceremony, injera, Bole airport, solar, geothermal and wind power, terraces, teff, rivers, drought, youth climate action, health and classrooms. Each is cropped to 800×500 WebP (≈48 KB) and lazy-loaded.
- **Honesty rules:** photos show real places and generic events, never COP32 itself. No logos or brand liveries, no close-up portraits, and no real public figures. Real photos are **never** paired with invented speaker names; speaker avatars stay illustrated (D56).
- **Attribution:** `#/menu/credits` (Profile & Settings → Photo credits) lists title, author, licence and source link for every photo, and notes that they were cropped and resized. Data is in `prototype/credits.js`.
- **Data saver:** with Data saver on, cards fall back to the lightweight illustrations (no photo downloads).
- **Offline:** photos are cached by the service worker as they are viewed.

## 8d. Name and mark: Lemlem (D58, 2026-10-05)
- **Name:** Lemlem (ለምለም, “lush, green, flourishing”), written “Lemlem · COP32” in the header and store name; home-screen label “Lemlem”. “COP32” stays in the name while this is a prototype (founder decision); the “Independent · not an official COP32 product” label stays on every screen.
- **Mark:** a seedling (a stem plus two leaves with midribs; the larger leaf on the right and lighter) rising over two highland horizons, with a low sun at top left, on a vertical teal gradient (#1C7478 → #0B4247) with a soft top-left glow. Leaf greens: #7FCB3E → #B9EC7E and #A6E26B → #E2F7C6. Sun: #FFC27A → #E8862A. Original artwork; not derived from any COP32 or UNFCCC mark.
- **Files:** `docs/design/brand/lemlem-mark.svg` (full-bleed master), `lemlem-mark-maskable.svg` (seedling and sun scaled to the 80% safe zone for Android masks), `lemlem-icon-512.png`; the prototype uses `prototype/icons/` (favicon.svg, favicon-32, icon-192/512, maskable-512, apple-touch-icon).
- **Lockup:** 30px rounded mark + “Lemlem” (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 800, −0.015em) + a small “COP32” pill (primarySoft). Below 380px the pill hides; the mark and name stay.
- **Clear space and minimum size:** keep at least ¼ of the mark's width clear around it; minimum 24px on screen (the seedling still reads at 16px in the favicon).

## 9. How the prototype (Track D v2) uses this
`prototype/build.py` generates CSS custom properties from `tokens.json`; `prototype/styles.css` implements the components (`.group`/`.row` grouped list, `.lt` large title, `.nav` translucent bar, `.segc` segmented control, `.cap` capsules, `.notice`, `.pill`, `.tile`, `.hero`, `.switch`). The prototype is the first consumer and therefore the first test of the spec. Header change (D53): the ☰ menu became a **profile button** next to the language switch that opens Profile & Settings (`#/menu`), which also holds Learn, Library, Archive, Help and About. The routes are unchanged.
